Paper Replica Figure 1: Logistic Regression CIs & Paper Table Replicas

Methodology & Presentation

This report presents Paper Replica Figure 1 logistic regression plots alongside color-coded replica tables formatted identically to Table 1 (Numbers & Names) and Table 8 (Cities) from the paper:

  • Paper Replica Figure 1 Error Bars: Logistic regression coefficients transformed into centered probabilities \(\left( \frac{e^\beta}{1 + e^\beta} - 0.5 \right)\). Use the toggle button below to switch interactively between Standard 95% CIs (\(z=1.96\)) and Bonferroni-Adjusted CIs (\(1 - \alpha/m\)).
  • Paper Replica Tables (Table 1 & Table 8): Formatted win fractions (e.g. 0.70***) with coolwarm_r color gradients based on distance from 0.5. Significance stars reflect Bonferroni-corrected \(p\)-values across \(m=183\) cell tests (1-sample t-test per pair win rates against 0.5; *** \(p_{\text{Bonf}} \lt 0.001\), ** \(p_{\text{Bonf}} \lt 0.01\), * \(p_{\text{Bonf}} \lt 0.05\)).
  • Low-Data Row Italics: Rows where valid item pairs are \(\lt 50\%\) are displayed with their active percentage e.g. Prime (28%) and formatted in italics, matching the paper.
  • Purple Border Highlight (🟪): Cells enclosed in a Purple Border indicate cells whose significance star level changed after Bonferroni correction (e.g., downgraded from *** to **/*, or from * to no star). Hover over any purple cell to see instant tooltip popups with exact uncorrected \(p_{\text{raw}}\) vs. Bonferroni-adjusted \(p_{\text{Bonf}}\) values.
  • Bonferroni-Corrected Details: Expandable model-by-model tables providing exact Log-Odds \(\beta\), SE, z-score, Raw vs Bonferroni-adjusted \(p\)-values (\(p_{\text{Bonf}} = \min(1.0, m \times p_{\text{raw}})\)), and both 95% CI & Bonferroni CI bounds.

3. Mixed-Effects Model (GLMM) & Variance Decomposition (Click to Expand)

Rebuttal Context & Variance Disentanglement

"The design is fully crossed — every unique pair is evaluated under all 50 prompts and both orders — so per-prompt win rates are computed over an identical set of pairs, and pair-to-pair differences cannot masquerade as prompt effects. The remaining question is prompt effects vs. sampling noise, which is what the Levene's test addresses (rejecting the sampling-only null at p<0.001 for all 21 distributions). A mixed-effects model with crossed prompt and pair random effects is indeed the cleaner formulation..."

Variance Component Breakdown (Crossed Random Effects)

Total per-prompt win rate variance is decomposed into: Prompt Variance (\(\sigma^2_{\text{prompt}}\)), Item-Pair Variance (\(\sigma^2_{\text{pair}}\)), and Sampling / Residual Noise. Levene's \(W\) statistic tests whether prompt variance significantly exceeds pure sampling noise (\(H_0: \sigma^2_{\text{prompt}} = 0\)).
